title: Replace the coarse shell norm by a spectral-gap Duhamel bound
question: Can finite-time bond influence be controlled directly by the spectral-gap-weighted commutator of the moved doubled witness, avoiding a separate operator-norm factor?
method: Use the B spectral decomposition and the exact coefficient identity ||U_t* X U_t-X||_HS^2=sum_ab |exp(i t(lambda_a-lambda_b))-1|^2 ||P_a X P_b||_HS^2.
Apply |exp(i y)-1|<=|y| to obtain the finite-time Duhamel bound ||U_t* X U_t-X||_HS <= |t| ||[B,X]||_HS.
Use Hilbert--Schmidt Cauchy with a density omega to bound the state trace by ||omega||_HS times the same Duhamel quantity, without assuming [omega,B]=0.
Remove B-commuting blocks first with the R-364 spectral pinching, then check doubled bond-unitary factorisation and the spectral formula on every R-362 finite prefix.
Formalize the finite spectral coefficient, gap-square nonnegativity and block commutator reduction in Lean R365.
finding: R-365 advances FI-2b at finite time. Primary passes 777/777 and independent 776/776 over 256 contexts; integrated 49/49 and Lean R365 pass. Maximum spectral coefficient error is 1.505e-13, maximum phase identity error 6.178e-14, maximum Duhamel violation 7.006e-14, and maximum state-trace violation -3.206e-17. The largest finite-time/bound ratio is 0.999422, with maximum change 0.267414 against bound 0.267991. The spectral commutator remains nonzero with minimum nonzero norm 0.867344.
decision_reason: The spectral-gap form controls the actual finite-time bond unitary by energy differences and avoids multiplying a residual by a separate operator norm. It supplies an exact finite-time shell inequality and a dimension-free density-trace corollary, while leaving the commutator norm's asymptotic uniformity as the decisive open obligation.

adversarial_review.check: The lane derives and checks the U_t* X U_t phase factors in the same orientation as the finite-time difference.
The tensor-product bond unitary is compared directly with exp(-i t B), not assumed from notation.
The state-trace corollary uses Hilbert--Schmidt Cauchy and ||omega||_HS<=1; no state-generator commutation is used.
Some contexts have a numerical zero, but the minimum nonzero spectral commutator is positive and no universal cancellation is claimed.
The finite Duhamel constant one does not control ||[B,X]||_HS uniformly in cutoff, volume, source, prefix or shape.
No common alpha, local collar, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure follows.
Lean proves finite spectral algebra only; exponentials, matrix spectra and limits remain in the executable lanes.

next_action: Obtain a local modular or Lieb--Robinson estimate on the spectral-gap commutator norm uniform in source, cutoff, volume, prefix and exhaustion shape; register exact growth if unavailable.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite exact Duhamel reduction and actual-Q3 diagnostic. No uniform local collar, phase-weight theorem, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure follows.
no_overclaim: The finite-time spectral-gap inequality has constant one, but the commutator norm can still grow with the regulator and no QFT limit is established.
